title: EFX and Pareto optimality for personalized bi-valued goods
statement: For arbitrary finite numbers of agents and goods with additive values v_i(g)∈{a_i,b_i}, where each agent has its own fixed positive pair a_i>b_i>0, determine whether a complete EFX allocation always exists that is also Pareto optimal among complete allocations. EFX requires v_i(X_i)≥v_i(X_j\{g}) for all i,j,g∈X_j; Pareto optimality excludes any allocation weakly improving every agent and strictly improving one.
source_locator: Jin and Tao, Sections 2-5; He and Tao, Section 6; Lin, Wu and Zhou, Theorem 3.5 and Example 3.6.
status_basis: Jin and Tao pose exact simultaneous existence as open; He and Tao repeat this status. The later maximum-Nash-welfare result proves a tight approximation guarantee for that rule, not a resolution of exact EFX plus integral Pareto optimality. No later matching resolution was located.

revision_history.change: Expanded the existing candidate into a full card and added the maximum-Nash-welfare approximation result; retained the original question and ID.

plain_summary: Can indivisible goods always be shared so that envy disappears after removing any one good from another person's bundle, while no reassignment can benefit someone without harming another?
assumptions: Finitely many agents and goods; every good is assigned once and values are additive.
Each agent uses its own two strictly positive values. Ratios a_i/b_i may differ between agents.
Pareto comparisons are against complete integral allocations. Fractional reallocations are outside this target.
scope: Exact EFX together with integral Pareto optimality. EFX alone is established. Efficient computation is a further question if simultaneous existence holds; no restriction to a selected number of agents or ratio range is imposed here.
target: Prove simultaneous existence for all such instances or give one instance in which every EFX allocation is Pareto dominated.
success_criteria: An existence proof must satisfy both properties for the same complete allocation.
A counterexample must rule out every complete EFX allocation, not merely one algorithm's output.
State any restricted parameter class explicitly and report its result as partial progress.
known_results: Jin and Tao prove polynomial-time EFX existence. They also characterize Pareto optimality and distinguish integral from fractional ratios in its decision complexity.
Their Section 5 shows that maximum Nash welfare can fail exact EFX and that fractional Pareto optimality can be incompatible with EFX.
Lin, Wu and Zhou report a tight 2/3-EFX guarantee for maximum Nash welfare. Tightness of that rule does not rule out another allocation satisfying exact EFX and Pareto optimality.
prerequisites: Additive fair division, EFX and Pareto dominance.
Exact finite optimization and certificates of exhaustive coverage.
significance: Locates the boundary between a strong fairness guarantee and efficient use of resources in a simple heterogeneous-preference model.

relations.explanation: Both concern additive goods. This entry restricts each agent to two positive values and adds efficiency; the four-agent entry permits general values and requires fairness alone.

requirements.experiment: None for this existence question. People's acceptance of EFX is an empirical matter outside its scope.
requirements.data: Published definitions and exact valuation matrices for any future finite study.
requirements.compute: Unmeasured. A fixed n-agent, m-good instance has n^m complete assignments. Exact small-instance checking may be manageable; growth and general Pareto verification can be expensive.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Additive, strictly positive, personalized two-value preferences and integral complete assignment.

methods: Study the source's Pareto characterization and matching-based EFX construction.
Compare any proposed result with the published failures of maximum Nash welfare and fractional-market approaches.
obstacles: Fairness and efficiency can each hold for different allocations.
Checking one EFX witness does not establish Pareto optimality.
A fractional Pareto improvement is not necessarily an integral one.

steps: Check positivity, the two-value condition and complete assignment.
Evaluate EFX using the potentially envious agent's values for both bundles.
For a finite negative result, give coverage of all EFX allocations and an integral Pareto dominator for each.
Independently check exact data and any symmetry or pruning argument.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Moderate for a small fully enumerated instance; high for a general theorem or a large exhaustive certificate.
validation.statement_alignment: Goods, personalized ratios and integral Pareto optimality are essential. Approximate EFX, chores or fractional efficiency answer different questions.

known_attempts: The source records failed routes through maximum Nash welfare and fractional market equilibria. No project attempt has been run.
unresolved_checks: Refresh the literature before selecting a special case or claiming novelty.
Clarify the inconsistent manuscript and repository dates for arXiv:2610.00122v1.
Independently audit any source theorem used in a new proof.
